extracted.intended_audience: IP attorneys, patent agents, law firm managers, and IP-practice administrators
extracted.subtask_description: Summarize and report quantitative metrics about IP practice economics and firm characteristics (staffing, billing, outsourcing, insurance, litigation/arbitration costs) as collected in AIPLA's 2023 Economic Survey. Intended to inform benchmarking and planning for IP legal practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correlation between amount at risk and attorney hours
rubrics_metrics.description: More than eight in 10 respondents (81.8%) report that there is a strong correlation between the amount at risk in a trade secret misappropriation action and the overall attorney hours required to litigate the action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Survey finding indicating that case stakes are strongly associated with required attorney hours; used as an explanatory metric when estimating litigation staffing and budgets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total cost of asserting vs defending trade secret misappropriation action
rubrics_metrics.description: A similar proportion (81.3%) indicate that the total cost of asserting a trade secret misappropriation action is about the same as the total cost of defending such an action. The average cost of asserting as reported by others is 90.6% of the cost to defend.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a benchmark ratio (asserting ≈90.6% of defending) for budgeting plaintiff-side vs defendant-side trade-secret litigation costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total cost of arbitration compared to litigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Approaching 40.0% of respondents reported that the total cost of resolving a dispute through arbitration compared to resolving a comparable dispute through litigation is about the same (38.8%). Other respondents reported that the average cost of arbitration as a percent of the cost of litigation was 77.7%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these percentages to benchmark ADR cost expectations; indicates arbitration often (but not always) costs less than litigation—average ~77.7% of litigation cost per respondents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frequency/reason mediation or arbitration initiated
rubrics_metrics.description: Mediation/arbitration was initiated most often in 2022 based on the terms of the contract (47.5%); mandated by a court in 2022 was 29.2%; initiated voluntarily by parties 23.3%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows common triggers for ADR—contract clauses are the leading cause; useful when assessing dispute-resolution clauses and likely forum-selection outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost of mediation (by case stage and amount at risk)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tables and quartiles show mediation costs and case-management costs at different stages (initial case management; incl. discovery, motions, claim construction; incl. pre to post-trial & appeal) and by amounts at risk (e.g., $10–$25M, >$25M).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides percentile benchmarks (1st quartile, median, mean, 3rd quartile) for mediation and litigation phase costs to inform budgeting by case stage and exposure level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number and distribution of attorneys in firms
rubrics_metrics.description: Responding firms reported distributions of firm size (one, two, 3–5, 6–10, 11–30, 31–100, 101+ attorneys) and medians/averages for counts of equity partners/shareholders, partner-track attorneys, non-partner track, of counsel, contract/part-time, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these staffing distributions and medians (e.g., median total number of attorneys 7.5 in 2022) for benchmarking hiring, promotion, and firm-size comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office locations and space plans
rubrics_metrics.description: 66.9% of responding firms reported having one major office location; 94.2% do not have plans to close any major office locations in 2023 or 2024; average number of office locations was 3.7 in 2022; 24.0% reported they have reduced or are planning to reduce office space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Benchmarks for office footprint planning and consolidation decisions post-pandemic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remote work prevalence and intensity
rubrics_metrics.description: In 2022, an average of 56.8% of employees worked remotely; for 2023 an average of 53.8% was reported. Survey tables show percent of individuals who worked remotely (82.9% of respondents), percent time remote (means/medians), miles from office, and plans to continue remote work in 2023 (81.7% plan to).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed remote-work metrics (percent working remote, percent time remote, distance) to guide hybrid policies and workspace needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Percent of practice by billings that is IP
rubrics_metrics.description: Approximately eight in 10 (79.7%) say that IP accounted for three-quarters or more of their practice in 2022.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use as a benchmark of practice concentration for firms identifying as IP-specialized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promotions, turnover, and hiring channels
rubrics_metrics.description: Medians for promotions in 2022 (e.g., associates promoted to non-equity partner median 2.0; to equity partner median 1.0); median of 4.0 IP professionals left and 4.0 joined the firm in 2022. More than eight in 10 (82.1%) indicated less than 25% of attorneys were hired through a recruiter; when used, median fee paid was 23.0% of salary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Benchmarks for annual mobility, promotion rates, and recruiter usage/fees for workforce planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gender composition of IP attorneys and trend
rubrics_metrics.description: Based on averages, 71.2% males and 28.5% females (0.2% “other”); percentage of males has declined slightly compared to earlier years (e.g., ~75% in 2011/2013).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diversity benchmark for gender composition and multi-year trend monitoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethnicity composition of IP attorneys and trend
rubrics_metrics.description: Based on averages, 77.9% White/Caucasian, 13.5% Asian/Pacific Islander, 3.2% Hispanic/Latino, 1.9% Black/African American, 1.8% Mixed Race, 0.2% North American Indian/Native Canadian, 1.5% Other. Historical charts 2011–2023 included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diversity benchmark for ethnicity composition and trend analysis across survey waves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outsourcing of IP practice services
rubrics_metrics.description: Prosecution services not often outsourced (96.8% do not outsource). Searching outsourced in the U.S. by 35.0% of firms; annuity payments outsourced in the U.S. by 32.6% and abroad by 16.7%; international filings outsourced abroad by 39.6%. Docketing, litigation services, paralegal support, IDSs have high 'not outsourced' percentages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational benchmarking for which IP tasks firms outsource and at what rates—useful for staffing and vendor decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of formal training provided
rubrics_metrics.description: Other than one-on-one mentorship, firms most often provide formal training on practice skills (e.g., claim drafting, case law review) 81.0% and business development 77.6%; personal growth 48.3%; team dynamics 44.8%; leadership 41.4%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on common internal training priorities for IP practices and allocation of training resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Activities receiving billable-hour credit
rubrics_metrics.description: Activities for which associates received billable-hour credit: pro bono work 48.5%; marketing 22.1%; bar association participation 15.8%; professional organization participation 15.6%; newsletter drafting 13.8%; RFP process 13.8%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy benchmarking for what non-matter work firms credit as billable for associates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Associate starting salary and summer monthly pay
rubrics_metrics.description: Median 2022 monthly summer pay was $10,000. The reported median current starting salary for first-year associates was $135,000 (higher than $125,000 in 2021). Salary increases with firm size (e.g., median for 101+ attorneys $192,500).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compensation benchmarking by firm size for recruiting and budgeting; historical trend data provided (2004–2022).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent agents and IP support-staff counts and salaries
rubrics_metrics.description: Median number of USPTO-registered patent agents in 2022 was 3.0 (average 5.2). Median number technical advisors/assistants 2.0 (avg 8.0). Median number paralegals/legal assistants 4.0 (avg 8.7). Median patent agent salary $121,122 (avg $131,849); median IP paralegal $80,000 (avg $79,149). Median non-billable support staff devoted to IP was 4.0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staffing and compensation benchmarks for non-attorney IP roles used in headcount planning and salary-setting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution of non-billable support staff per firm and per attorney
rubrics_metrics.description: Distribution percentages for counts of non-billable support staff (e.g., one: 28.6%, two: 9.5%, 21+ :20.0%); median number per firm 4.0; median number of non-billable support staff per IP attorney 0.5 (avg 0.7).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Benchmarks for support-staff-to-attorney ratios as a staffing metric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Average composition of 2022 IP billings by service type
rubrics_metrics.description: For all respondents, 54.2% of 2022 IP billings, on average, were for patent applications and prosecution; 17.7% for trademark applications and prosecution; 14.8% for litigation (not including post-grant actions at the USPTO); PTAB/TTAB proceedings 2.7%; licensing 3.2%; copyright registration apps 1.8%; privacy/cybersecurity 0.7%; other IP work 5.0%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revenue-mix benchmark to compare firm service-line concentration and guide business development priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total billings per attorney and average billing rates
rubrics_metrics.description: Median total 2022 billing per attorney $413,793; average $465,684. Median average 2022 billing rate for IP work $420 (average $447); largest firms (101+) reported highest median billing rates ($621 for IP work). Detailed quartiles by firm-size provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use as hour-rate and productivity benchmarks (billings per attorney and hourly billing rates) when setting rates and evaluating profitability by firm size.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collections-to-billings ratio and overhead percentage
rubrics_metrics.description: Ratio of firm collections to firm billings in 2022 was 93.6%. Overhead as a percent of total 2022 collections averaged 32.2% for responding firms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key financial-performance benchmarks for evaluating collections efficiency and overhead burden relative to collections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Average percent change in billings and revenue (2021→2022)
rubrics_metrics.description: The average percent change in billings for IP legal services from 2021 to 2022 was 11.0%. The average percent change in revenue for IP legal services from 2021 to 2022 was 11.2%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Year-over-year growth benchmarks to set expectations for revenue and billing changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liability insurance coverage and costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Median total maximum liability insurance coverage in 2022 was $4,000,000 (same as prior four surveys). Median maximum per-claim coverage $2,000,000. Median total deductible $25,000 and $15,000 deductible per claim. Median liability insurance cost per attorney in 2022 was $4,800. Cyber liability included in general liability value by 34.3% of firms; of those without cyber included, 51.6% reported they do not have cyber liability insurance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insurance coverage and cost benchmarks to inform risk-management purchasing and budgeting for professional liability and cyber coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remote-work and full-time employment metrics (individual-level)
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual-response tables: percent who worked remotely in 2022 (82.9% of all individuals), percent planning to work remotely in 2023 (81.7%), means and medians for percent time remote (e.g., mean 65.8% of time remote for those who worked remotely in 2022; median 75%), miles distance from office, and percent working full-time as defined by firm (91.7% yes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Granular individual-level metrics to shape HR policies regarding remote work schedules, full-time/part-time classification, and geographic dispersion.
